subtype: Approach: seeking advice from an older trusted person [Action]
passage: I'm Aleena, and for weeks I told myself it was romance. Pankaj kept saying, “If you really liked me you'd send one photo. Everyone does.” When I said no, he sulked for two days, then asked again. I felt confused and guilty, like I was failing a test I hadn't studied for. I told Ojas bhaiya, my older cousin, on a Sunday walk, and he went quiet, then said, “Real liking doesn't keep pushing after a no.” That evening I told Amma everything. She didn't scold me. She held my hand, called me her brave girl, said none of it was my fault, and phoned the school counsellor that same evening to arrange a talk. I still remember what bhaiya said: pressure isn't romance. It's a warning.

qa.a: Aleena told Ojas bhaiya, her older cousin, on a Sunday walk.

qa.q: What was Aleena feeling while Pankaj kept pushing?
qa.a: Aleena felt confused and guilty, as if she were failing a test she hadn't studied for.

qa.q: What could Aleena do if Pankaj keeps messaging her?
qa.a: Aleena could stop replying, keep the messages, and let Amma and the counsellor guide the next steps.

qa.q: How might Amma have felt on hearing it?
qa.a: Amma was probably worried and protective yet calm, since she held Aleena's hand and acted the same evening.

grounding: Confused by a boyfriend's pressure to send photos, a teen asks an older cousin and then her mother, and learns such pressure is a warning, not romance.

subtype: Approach: seeking advice from an older trusted person [Action]
passage:
Note to myself, Friday night.
Aparna knocked on my door at ten, holding her phone like it was hot. "Sameera told me to come to you, Ammi. Tonight." Then it came out: for two weeks Irfan, the boy she has been seeing from tuition, has been asking her to send photos, the kind she does not want to send. When she refused, he said it proves she doesn't love him. She wondered if this was just how relationships are, and asked her cousin first.
I kept my voice low. I told her this is not her fault, that she did the right thing coming to me, and that pushing like this is a warning sign, not love. She cried a little, then looked lighter.
Together we saved the messages and muted his chat. Before she slept, I messaged her class teacher asking for a call first thing tomorrow.

qa.q: Who told Aparna to go to Ammi?
qa.a: Her cousin Sameera told her to come to Ammi that night.

qa.q: What was Aparna feeling when she knocked on the door?
qa.a: Aparna was anxious and confused, holding the phone as if it were hot and half-believing such pressure was normal in relationships.

qa.q: What else could help Aparna in the coming days?
qa.a: Aparna could keep the saved messages, let the class teacher or school counsellor help, and lean on Sameera and Ammi if Irfan keeps pushing.

qa.q: How does Ammi see Irfan's pressure?
qa.a: Ammi sees it clearly as a warning sign, not romance, and responds calmly that same night so Aparna feels safe rather than blamed.

grounding: Shows a confused teen asking an older cousin and then her mother about pressure to send photos, and learning it is a warning sign, not romance.

subtype: Approach: seeking advice from an older trusted person [Action]
passage:
Sunday
Karan asked again tonight. Third time this week. "If you really trusted me you'd send one. Just one. Everybody does." I kept thinking maybe I'm being a baby about it.
So I called Bidisha Didi, because she's in college and she never laughs at me. She listened, then said, "Nikku, when someone keeps pushing after you say no, that's not romance. That's a warning." She told me to talk to Mummy today, not someday.
I almost didn't. But after dinner I showed Mummy the chat. Her face went still and I thought I was in trouble. Instead she hugged me and said, "You did nothing wrong by telling me." We took screenshots together and she muted his number. Tomorrow we're meeting my class teacher, together.
I feel shaky but lighter.
Nikita

qa.q: What did Bidisha Didi call the pushing?
qa.a: She said it is not romance; it is a warning.

qa.q: Why did Nikita almost not show Mummy the chat?
qa.a: Nikita was scared of being in trouble and even worried the whole thing was babyish.

qa.q: What else could Nikita do if Karan tries again through another app?
qa.a: Nikita could stop replying, keep screenshots, and tell Mummy or the class teacher straight away, just like this time.

qa.q: How does Mummy respond to what she sees?
qa.a: Mummy is clearly shaken but stays gentle, telling Nikita that speaking up was right, saving the chat and planning to see the class teacher together.

grounding: Illustrates a teen pressured by a boyfriend to send photos seeking advice from an older cousin and then the mother, and learning that such pressure is a warning.
